payload.rationale: Historically, US housing starts have frequently exceeded the 1.300M annualized rate, averaging between 1.4M and 1.6M during the 2020-2022 boom and hovering near 1.3M-1.4M during the higher interest rate environment of 2023-2024. Assuming interest rates stabilize or decline by 2026, builder activity is likely to be supported by pent-up demand and a structural deficit in the US housing supply, making a figure above 1.300M more likely than not. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is if the US economy enters a severe recession in 2026 or if mortgage rates remain restrictively high, depressing new construction below the 1.300M mark. The strongest reason this estimate could be too low is if aggressive rate cuts and strong demographic demand trigger a robust housing boom, pushing starts well above 1.5M, making 1.300M a very easily cleared hurdle.
limitations: Lack of macroeconomic data for the 2024-2026 period.
